t.4.34.1: To Lakṣmaṇa, the son of Sumitrā, who was speaking thus and seemed ablaze with fiery energy, Tārā, whose face was like the lord of the stars, spoke.
t.4.34.2: Lakṣmaṇa, he should not be spoken to thus; this lord of the monkeys does not deserve to hear harsh words, especially from your mouth.
t.4.34.3: Sugrīva is surely not ungrateful, nor deceitful, nor cruel; O hero, the lord of the monkeys is not one who speaks untruth, nor is he crooked.
t.4.34.5: O scorcher of foes, it is by Rāma's grace that Sugrīva has obtained here fame, the lasting kingship of the monkeys, Rumā, and me as well.
t.4.34.4: O hero, this heroic monkey Sugrīva has not forgotten the service Rāma rendered him, a deed in battle that others would have found hard to accomplish.
t.4.34.6: Having formerly been made to lie in great misery, and now having obtained this supreme happiness, he does not recognize that the appointed time has come, just like the sage Viśvāmitra.
t.4.34.8: For even the mighty and splendid Viśvāmitra, foremost among those who know the right time, did not perceive when the time had come; how much less, then, one who is an ordinary man!
t.4.34.7: Lakṣmaṇa, it is said that the great sage Viśvāmitra, righteous of soul, remained attached to Ghṛtācī for ten years, and ah, he thought it but a brief moment.
t.4.34.9: O Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma ought to forgive him here, for he has given way to the nature of the body, is worn out by long hardship, and is not yet sated with pleasures.
t.4.34.10: Dear Lakṣmaṇa, you should not fall under the sway of anger rashly, like a common man, without first ascertaining the true state of the matter.
t.4.34.11: For men like you, O bull among men, who are endowed with goodness, do not rashly fall under the sway of anger without first reflecting.
t.4.34.12: O knower of dharma, I earnestly beseech you to be gracious on Sugrīva's behalf; let this great fury that has arisen from anger be cast aside.
t.4.34.13: Rumā, me, the kingdom of the monkeys, and wealth, grain and riches, all these Sugrīva would give up for the sake of what is dear to Rāma; such is my conviction.
t.4.34.14: Having slain Rāvaṇa in battle, Sugrīva will unite Rāghava with Sītā, as the moon is united with Rohiṇī.
t.4.34.16: Without slaying those invincible rākṣasas who can take any form at will, Rāvaṇa, by whom that Maithilī was carried off, cannot be slain.
t.4.34.15: In Laṅkā, it is said, there are rākṣasas numbering thousands of hundreds of crores, and thirty-six ayutas, and thousands, and hundreds as well.
t.4.34.18: Thus did Vālī, the lord of the monkeys, relate it, for he was well informed. The source of this knowledge is not clear to me; I speak only from having heard it from him.
t.4.34.17: O Lakṣmaṇa, they cannot be slain in battle by one who has no allies, and above all Sugrīva alone cannot slay Rāvaṇa of cruel deeds.
t.4.34.19: Indeed, for the sake of aiding you, the foremost of the monkeys have been sent forth to bring very many monkeys and leaders of monkey troops for the battle.
t.4.34.20: Awaiting those valiant and mighty monkeys for the accomplishment of Rāghava's purpose, this lord of the monkeys does not set out.
t.4.34.21: But, O Saumitri, the arrangement has been made by Sugrīva just as before: today all those mighty monkeys are to arrive.
t.4.34.22: Thousands of crores of bears and hundreds of golāṅgūla monkeys will come to you today, so cast off your anger, O subduer of foes. And many crores of monkeys of blazing energy will come as well, O Kākutstha.
t.4.34.23: For, seeing this face of yours and beholding your eyes red as blood with anger, the wives of the foremost of monkeys find no peace, for all of us are seized with dread of that earlier terror.
